questions.question: By default, how long does an Apex callout have before it times out?
options: 10 seconds
60 seconds (10 seconds minimum, 120 seconds maximum, configurable)
There is no timeout
5 minutes
questions.explanation: The default callout timeout is 10 seconds, but you can set `setTimeout()` anywhere from 1 ms up to 120,000 ms (120 seconds). Many teams use 60s as a safe default for slower external APIs.

questions.question: Why can't you make an HTTP callout directly from a trigger?
options: Triggers run inside the same transaction as the DML that fired them, and callouts aren't allowed while there's an open transaction with pending changes — you must go through an asynchronous context like @future or Queueable
Triggers don't have access to the Http class
It is technically possible but Salesforce discourages it for style reasons only
Callouts from triggers are allowed in all cases with no extra steps
questions.explanation: Salesforce blocks synchronous callouts from a trigger's transaction (you'd get a "callout from a trigger context" error). Hand the callout off to a @future(callout=true) or Queueable method instead.

questions.question: What does a Named Credential give you that hardcoding an endpoint URL and API key in Apex does not?
options: Nothing extra — they behave identically
Salesforce stores and injects the authentication for you, so secrets never appear in your Apex code or get exposed via debug logs
Named Credentials make the callout run faster
Named Credentials remove the need for remote site settings entirely in every scenario
questions.explanation: A Named Credential centralizes the endpoint and handles authentication at the platform level, so your Apex code never touches raw credentials — safer and easier to rotate.

questions.question: A callout to a partner API intermittently returns a 503. What's the most robust way to handle this in Apex?
options: Ignore the failure silently and move on
Catch the exception/non-2xx response and apply a retry strategy (e.g. re-enqueue via Queueable with a limited retry count), rather than retrying forever in a tight loop
Always retry immediately in an infinite while loop within the same transaction
Increase the org-wide API limit so 503s stop happening
questions.explanation: 503s are often transient. A bounded retry (ideally with backoff, done asynchronously via Queueable) handles real-world flakiness without risking runaway loops or governor limit exhaustion.

questions.question: Which governor limit applies specifically to outbound HTTP callouts in a single Apex transaction?
options: Maximum of 100 callouts per transaction, and 120 seconds total cumulative callout time
Unlimited callouts as long as you use a Named Credential
Exactly 1 callout per transaction
Callouts don't count against any governor limit
questions.explanation: Apex enforces a maximum of 100 callouts per transaction and a combined 120-second ceiling across all callouts in that transaction — design batch sizes and timeouts with this in mind.
